# Ⅲ.Reading Comprehension (50 points)
Section A
Passage 1
# 【文章大意】
关于大一学生的调查告诉我们为什么大多数学生都上大学： $8 8 \%$ 想要“一个找到一份好工作的更好的机会”， $8 1 \%$ 想要变“富有和有钱”。然而，现在大多数学生不能实现这些目标。有一个仔细的研究发现，在校大学生在学习上花费的时间更少了——从 20 世纪 60年代早期的每周 25 小时变成了现在的 15 小时。
学习也能导致更好的学习成绩。获得更好的学习成绩意味着变得“有钱”的更高的机会。一份关于毕业 15 年的 20000 名校友的研究发现了下面的结果。那些班级前三名的学生比中间三名的学生挣得多得多。中间三名的学生又比倒数三名的学生挣得多。不必惊奇，那些在大学里成绩不好的人都希望他们能够在学校学习更多。
学生是应该独自学习还是和别人一起学习这个问题比较复杂。如果老师把问题留给学生解决，如果学生首先尝试自己学习，小组学习往往是有帮助的。但是仅仅和同学在一起而不单独学习似乎不利于学习。在选课方面，很多学生更喜欢作业少、评分容易的课程。
然而，选择难度更大、阅读时间更长、论文更多的课程有助于提高学习。
在大学里，仍然有大量的时间来玩。然而，研究人员再次发现，并非所有的户外活动都是有益的。一般来说，活动，如参加学生组织和与同学交谈可以更有成效。
最后，大学是一个美妙的地方，有新的兴趣，丰富你的经验，并设定你的目标。这样做的时候，你可能会重新考虑“富有和富有”是否应该是你在大学学习的主要原因。据几位调查人员称，追求金钱的人通常对他们的生活不太满意。也许他们更容易忽视更重要的事情，如家庭，朋友和工作。
D. How long do you intend to stay?

Surveys about freshman tell us why most students go to college: $8 8 \%$ want a “better chance for a good job,” and $8 1 \%$ want to be “rich and wealthy.” However, most students today cannot reach these goals. One careful study has discovered that the undergraduates are spending less time in study —from about 25 hours per week in the early 1960s to below 15 hours today.
Studying also leads to better college grades. To have better grades means higher chances of becoming “rich and wealthy.” One study of 20,000 alumni (校友) 15 years after their graduation found the following results. Those who were in the top third of the class earned a lot more than those in the middle third. The middle third earned more than classmates in the bottom third. Not surprisingly, those whose grades were not good at college wished they had studied more in school.
Whether students should study alone or with others is more complicated. If the teachers leave problems for students to solve, group study is often helpful if students first try to study by themselves. But simply getting together with classmates without first studying alone seems bad for learning. In choosing courses, many students prefer classes with a little homework and easy grading. Yet taking harder courses with longer readings and more papers helps to increase learning.
In college, there will still be plenty of time for fun. Once again, however, researchers find that not all outside activities are good. In general, activities, such as participating in student organizations and talking with classmates can be more fruitful.
Last but not least, college is a wonderful place to have new interests, enrich your experience, and set your goals. In doing so, you might think again about whether “being rich and wealthy” should be your main reason for studying in college. According to several investigators, money seekers are usually less satisfied with their lives. Maybe they are more likely to neglect things that are more important, such as family, friends and work.

# Passage 2
# 【文章大意】
当你得知树木像动物一样互相交流并把财富传给下一代时，你会感到惊讶吗?
UBC 教授 Simard 解释了为什么树木比我们想象的要复杂得多。尽管查尔斯·达尔文认为树木是为了适者生存而竞争，但西玛德证明了他的观点是多么的错误。事实上，事实正好相反;树木通过它们的合作和支持生存下来，“取决于谁需要”传递必要的营养。
氮和碳通过绵延数英里的地下真菌网络共享，确保森林生态系统中的所有树木都能提供和接收到适量的氮和碳，以保持它们的健康。这个隐藏系统的运作方式与我们大脑中的神经元网络非常相似，当一棵树被破坏时，它会影响到所有的树。
Simard 谈到了“母树”，通常是所有其他树木赖以生存的最大最古老的植物。她解释了垂死的树木如何将财富传递给下一代，将重要的矿物质传递给幼树，使它们能够继续生长。当人类砍伐“母树”时，却没有意识到这些高度复杂的“树社会”或它们赖以生存的网络，我们正在减少整个森林的生存机会。
“我们对此毫不在意，”Simard 悲伤地说。“枯死的树在枯死之前会把营养转移到小树身上，但我们从不给它们机会。”如果我们能把这个信息传达给林业，我们就能对未来的环境保护工作产生巨大的影响。
D. Because they take less care of families and friends.

Would it surprise you to learn that, like animals, trees communicate with each other and transmit their wealth to the next generation?
UBC Professor Simard explains how trees are much more complex than most of us ever imagined. Although Charles Darwin thought that trees are competing for survival of the fittest, Simard shows just how wrong he was. In fact, the opposite is true; trees survive through their co-operation and support, passing around necessary nutrition “depending on who needs it”.
Nitrogen (氮) and carbon are shared through miles of underground fungi (真菌) networks, making sure that all trees in the forest ecological system give and receive just the right amount to keep them all healthy. This hidden system works in a very similar way to the networks of neurons (神经元) in our brains, and when one tree is destroyed, it affects all.
Simard talks about “mother trees”, usually the largest and oldest plants on which all other trees depend. She explains how dying trees pass on the wealth to the next generation, transporting important minerals to young trees so they may continue to grow. When humans cut down “mother trees” with no awareness of these highly complex “tree societies” or the networks on which they feed, we are reducing the chances of survival for the entire forest.
“We didn’t take any notice of it,” Simard says sadly. “Dying trees move nutrition into the young trees before dying, but we never give them chance.” If we could put across the message to the forestry industry, we could make a huge difference towards our environmental protection efforts for the future.

# Section B
# 【文章大意】
宽恕是一种美德，但从来没有人说这是容易的。当有人深深地伤害了你时，要放下你的仇恨是极其困难的。然而，宽恕是可能的，它会对你的身心健康带来意想不到的好处。最近的一项研究显示，懂得宽恕的人更少悲伤、愤怒和压力，更充满希望。
你应该如何开始原谅?试试以下步骤:
冷静自己。尝试一种简单的压力管理技巧，让你的愤怒消失。
你可以做几次深呼吸，然后想想那些令你快乐的事情:自然界的美丽景色，或者你爱的人。
不要等别人道歉。很多时候，伤害你的人并不打算道歉。他们可能是想伤害你，或者他们看待事物的方式和你不一样。如果你等着别人来道歉，你可能会等很长时间。记住，宽恕并不一定意味着和让你难过的人重新成为朋友。
不要让冒犯你的人控制你。重新思考你的伤害会给伤害你的人力量。与其老是关注自己受到的伤害，还不如学着去寻找你身边的真善美。
试着从冒犯你的人的角度看问题。如果你了解冒犯你的人，你可能会意识到他或她的行为是出于无意识、恐惧，甚至是爱。你可能想从冒犯你的人的角度给自己写一封信。
不要忘记原谅自己。对有些人来说，原谅自己是最大的挑战，但如果你不原谅自己，你就会失去自信。
D. We couldn't make efforts for the future environmental protection.

# Ⅳ. Cloze (20 points)
# 【文章大意】
英语有句谚语:“笑是最好的药。”直到最近，很少有人把这句话当真。然而，现在医生们已开始研究笑及其对人体的影响。他们发现笑真的可以改善人们的健康。
人们进行了一些实验来研究笑对身体的影响。当医生检查他们的心脏、血压、呼吸和肌肉时，让人们观看有趣的电影。人们发现笑和体育锻炼有类似的效果。它会增加血压、心跳和呼吸;它还能锻炼面部、胃部甚至脚部的几组肌肉。如果笑可以锻炼身体，那一定是有益的。
其他测试表明，笑似乎能够减轻身体疼痛的影响。在一项实验中，医生让一组听不同广播节目的学生感到疼痛。忍受疼痛时间最长的一组是听搞笑节目的那一组。笑可以减轻疼痛的原因似乎是它有助于大脑中产生一种化学物质，这种化学物质可以减轻压力和疼痛。
由于这些发现，美国的一些医生现在开设了“大笑诊所”，通过鼓励病人笑来帮助他们改善病情。他们发现，即使他们的病人不是真的想笑，让他们微笑也足以产生与大笑类似的有益效果。

# V. Writing (15.points) 参考范文
# My view on happiness
With the development of our society, we are having much more happiness than ever before. For a student like me, happiness is never a thing far reaching. Instead, it is appearing in every corner of our life.
During the preparation of this examination, my parents, friends and teachers have given me tremendous help. I still remember the day when I was studying at night, I happened to notice that my mother was actually waiting for me in the living room with my dinner, without telling me.
There are many ways to reach happiness. Firstly, we should pay more attention on things around us. Secondly, happiness is not all about receiving but sometimes about giving.
Spend more time with families and friends; do volunteer works instead of always waiting for help. Only then, can we embrace happiness.

My view on happiness
With the development of our society, we are having much more happiness than ever before. For a student like me, happiness is never a thing far reaching. Instead, it is appearing in every corner of our life.
During the preparation of this examination, my parents, friends and teachers have given me tremendous help. I still remember the day when I was studying at night, I happened to notice that my mother was actually waiting for me in the living room with my dinner, without telling me.
There are many ways to reach happiness. Firstly, we should pay more attention on things around us. Secondly, happiness is not all about receiving but sometimes about giving.
Spend more time with families and friends; do volunteer works instead of always waiting for help. Only then, can we embrace happiness.
